clue.text: Ban on fruit drink in this part of the theatre?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a crush is a drink made from squeezed fruit, as in orange crush
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether fruit drinks are forbidden in a certain area of the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the charade signal: in an across clue the second piece follows the first. The question mark flags a definition that points at a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A crush bar is the theatre bar where the audience crowds in during the interval.

clue.text: Obtainable from Bari — cottage cheese, Italian style

indicators.note: letters obtainable from a phrase are taken out of a run of it

explanation.surface: Cottage cheese done the Italian way can be bought in Bari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cottage' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the end of the hidden run in baRI COTTAge. Bari is a port in southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian whey cheese, much like cottage cheese.

clue.text: Complaining, having an unsatisfactory ring?

definitions.meaning: a bell or note that tolls badly gives off a poor tone

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the phrase literally: something giving out a sound that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounding off is an idiom for voicing complaints loudly, and literally a sound that is off-key.

clue.text: Villain has trapped twin daughters in cove

indicators.note: in means the pair is placed inside the word for cove

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: twin means the single letter appears as a matched pair

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A villain holds two twin girls captive in a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twin' doubles the abbreviation for daughter, and 'in' sets the pair inside the inlet word.
explanation.definitionFit: A baddy is an informal word for the villain of a story or film.

clue.text: Art twice slipped on piano pedal

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first
slipped suggests the letters slide out of their places into a new order
twice means the word is taken two times over

parts.note: taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musician keeps slipping on the soft pedal of the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives ARTART, which 'slipped' rearranges into RATTRA; P follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-trap is a toothed bicycle pedal built to grip the rider's shoe.

clue.text: Youngster is given marks in art school

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or junior scout, a youngster
taken as written
M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A young pupil receives grades at an art college.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism was the early-twentieth-century movement in painting led by Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Operation in Normandy town capturing southern district

indicators.note: capturing means the town's name holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy, France
an area is a district

explanation.surface: A military operation in a French town seizes a district in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' sets the abbreviation for southern plus the district word inside the French town's name. Caen is the capital of Calvados in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caesarean is a surgical operation to deliver a baby through the abdomen.

clue.text: Only half the dairy produce

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: butter is a dairy product

explanation.surface: Someone receives a mere half share of the milk products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps BUT from BUTTER, dropping its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: But can mean only, as in 'she is but a child'.

clue.text: Defeat American, establishing record

definitions.meaning: in American slang, to beat someone soundly
old 78 rpm gramophone discs were made of this resin

explanation.walkthrough: 'establishing' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is US slang for a thrashing and also the resin used for old gramophone records.

clue.text: He acted with troupe, in a sensational twist

definitions.text: He acted with troupe, in a sensational twist

indicators.note: twist means the letters are wrung into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor performing with a company produces a dramatic surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a theatrical surprise while 'twist' rearranges HE ACTED and TROUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de theatre is a sudden, dramatic turn of events, originally on stage.

clue.text: Boringly conventional way to replace unreliable leader

indicators.note: to replace means one piece takes the place of a letter, here the leading one

parts.note: something dodgy is unreliable
ST, for street, is a common abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: A dull, traditional route is chosen to oust a dubious boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace unreliable leader' swaps ST in for D, the first letter of DODGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy describes dull, heavy, conservative people or writing.

clue.text: Expert in authentic English books should at least be this?

definitions.text: books should at least be this?

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: real means authentic
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist in genuine English literature expects volumes at least to be enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the expert inside the authentic word, with English added at the end. DAB as an expert is a British usage, short for dab hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Books ought at a minimum to be easy and pleasant to get through.

clue.text: Served up a drink containing a measure of speed, explosive drug

indicators.note: containing means the turned-round pieces hold another within
in a down clue, served up means the pieces are written upwards

parts.note: taken as written
tea is a drink
MPH, miles per hour, measures speed
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone serves a drink spiked with speed, a dangerous stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' writes 'a drink' upwards in this down clue, giving AETA; 'containing' puts the speed measure after its first letter. Speed is also street slang for this drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphetamine is a stimulant drug, known on the street as speed.

clue.text: Ugly building to west of main town

indicators.note: in an across clue, west of means placed to the left, so first

parts.note: a barn is a large, plain building
staple can mean main, as in a staple diet

explanation.surface: An eyesore stands to the west of the principal settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnstaple is a town in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon.

clue.text: Arranged nice chat with learner in one sort of college

indicators.note: with means the letter is added alongside
arranged means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A friendly talk was set up with a student at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' makes TECHNICA from NICE CHAT; L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical college teaches practical and vocational subjects.

clue.text: Group of scouts prepare for holiday?

definitions.meaning: a unit of Cub Scouts or Brownies
to fill a suitcase before going away

explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a group of young scouts, and to pack is to fill luggage before travel.

clue.text: Old house, one in a state

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient home with a single resident sits in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside HO, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is a state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Leader had name changed

indicators.note: changed means these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chief had his title altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges HAD NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A headman is the chief of a village or tribe.

clue.text: Service to give ex-PM royal status?

parts.note: to crown someone is to give them royal status
the Earl of Derby was a British Prime Minister three times in the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: A ceremony is held to make a former premier king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church ceremony but means a set of tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is fine porcelain, sold as dinner and tea services.

clue.text: Play with books and magazine

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
Hello! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A drama is staged with volumes and a glossy periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Refuse to have fuel inside centre of operations

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within another

parts.note: a base is a centre of operations
gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone declines to keep fuel stored in headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the waste pulp left after sugar cane is crushed.

clue.text: Henry gets the bird? That's appropriate

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry
a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Henry is hissed at, and someone thinks he deserves it.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF-INCH is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, to steal, which is 'appropriate' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang half-inch means pinch, so it means to steal or take.

clue.text: Dutch house in the shade

definitions.meaning: the royal family of the Netherlands
a colour between red and yellow

explanation.definitionFit: Orange is the Dutch royal house and also a colour.

clue.text: Yellow line drawn by darts player round end of bar

indicators.note: round means one piece surrounds another

parts.note: the oche is the line a darts player stands behind

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A darts player marks a yellow line round the end of the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts R, the last letter of 'bar', inside OCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and colour.

clue.text: Game one can't stand to win —- at the end, there's no score

definitions.text: Game one can't stand to win —- at the end, there's no score

parts.words: Game one can't stand to win —- at the end, there's no score
parts.note: a party game where the last player left with a seat wins, and the music stopping decides it rather than any points

explanation.walkthrough: 'can't stand' means cannot be left standing, and 'no score' plays on the music, or score, having stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is the party game in which players scramble for seats when the music stops.

clue.text: Realise it's the waves that can be heard

indicators.note: that can be heard means the word is said out loud

parts.note: the waves stand for the sea

explanation.surface: Someone understands it is the surf one can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA and SEE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to understand or realise, as in 'I see what you mean'.

clue.text: Open University's new decorative stamp

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a seal is an embossed stamp or emblem

explanation.surface: The Open University has a fresh ornamental emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' reads as the British distance-learning institution, but 'Open' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseal something is to open it by breaking its seal.

clue.text: Surprised to be awake?

explanation.definitionFit: Open-eyed describes both astonishment and being wakeful with eyes not closed.
